question: Should OpenClaw adopt a small inspect-only capability declaration first, or define a broader signed permission-and-enforcement contract spanning ClawHub installs, updates, and runtime tool access?
rationale: The correct schema location, what a declaration means, how existing skills upgrade, and whether registry verification, consent, and runtime controls are coupled are product and security-boundary choices that source inspection cannot safely settle.

options.title: Phase the declaration first
options.body: Adopt the narrow capability vocabulary proposed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/74594, keep it explicitly non-enforcing, and specify later phases separately.

options.title: Design the full contract first
options.body: Hold implementation until maintainers define the shared manifest, signing/provenance, consent, update-diff, and enforcement boundaries together.

options.title: Keep policy external
options.body: Rely on ClawHub verification and `security.installPolicy` integration without standardizing a core manifest for now.

recommendation.title: Phase the declaration first
recommendation.body: Adopt the narrow capability vocabulary proposed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/74594, keep it explicitly non-enforcing, and specify later phases separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The recorded review direction already frames this as a maintainer product and security decision, beyond a mechanical skills-path repair.
